title: Derived internal Hom into a K-injective and its derived global sections
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site that is small in the sense of [def-weil-size-convention] and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Use the category $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], its unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], Hom complexes $\mathcal Hom^\bullet$ [def-pur-hom-complex], and K-flat and K-injective complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pur-kinjective-complex]. The derived tensor product $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}N$ is represented by $\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal N^\bullet)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] for a K-flat complex $\mathcal P^\bullet$ representing $K$ and any complex $\mathcal N^\bullet$ representing $N$. Fix $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ and let $H_K:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O)$ be any right adjoint of $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}-$ . Let $\mathcal A^\bullet$ be any complex of $\mathcal O$-modules representing $K$, and let $\mathcal J^\bullet$ be a K-injective complex representing $M\in D(\mathcal O)$. Then:

1. There is an isomorphism $H_K(M)\cong\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal A^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet)$ in $D(\mathcal O)$, natural with respect to morphisms of K-injective complexes $\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$.
2. The derived global sections $R\Gamma(\mathcal C,H_K(M))$ [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology] are represented, in the derived category of abelian groups [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], by the complex of global morphisms $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(\mathcal A^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet)=\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal A^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet))$, whose degree-$n$ term is $\prod_{p\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal A^p,\mathcal J^{p+n})$, naturally with respect to morphisms of complexes $\mathcal A'^\bullet\to\mathcal A^\bullet$ and of K-injective complexes $\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$. In particular $H^n R\Gamma(\mathcal C,H_K(M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(K,M[n])$ for every integer $n$.

No boundedness of $K$ or $M$ and no flatness of $\mathcal A^\bullet$ is assumed.

proof.text: For tensorRightAdjoint_iso, use the existing ringed-site closed symmetric monoidal derived structure (lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal). Choose a K-flat resolution P of a representative L of K by lem-pc-kflat-resolution, and localize its augmentation to obtain QP ≅ K. The hypothesis model identifies Q ⋙ T with Tot(P tensor -) ⋙ Q. The closed structure's one-K-flat tensor comparison h.tensorIso, with h.tensorIso_naturality applied to (identity P,f), gives a natural isomorphism from that functor to Q ⋙ tensorLeft(QP). Transport through QP ≅ K. Fully faithful whiskering with the derived localization lifts the natural isomorphism to T ≅ tensorLeft(K). Compose with the symmetry tensorLeft(K) ≅ tensorRight(K). Uniqueness of right adjoints for the given adjunction and S.adjunction K gives H ≅ internalHom(K,-). All steps are implemented in Lean.

proof.text: Choose the functorial K-injective replacement I and its augmentation η. The comparison for derivedInternalHomOfUniverses identifies the localized Hom(A,I(-)) with the canonical derived internal Hom. On the subcategory of K-injectives, η is a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives; quasiIso_homComplex_mapOfUniverses therefore makes the comparison from Hom(A,J) to Hom(A,I(J)) invertible. This constructs the first natural representative isomorphism.

For every additive functor F between the relevant abelian categories, construct the canonical natural comparison Q(F(E)) → RF(Q(E)) using the homotopy-category factorization and rightDerivedFunctorUnit. This is invertible when E is K-injective by Mathlib's computation of a right derived functor on K-injectives. Apply this to global sections.

Choose a K-flat resolution p:P→A. Hom(P,J) is K-injective by the independent-universe Hom-K-injectivity theorem, whereas precomposition Hom(A,J)→Hom(P,J) is a quasi-isomorphism by quasiIso_homComplex_mapOfUniverses. The global Hom comparison identifies ordinary sections of these Hom complexes with the external Mathlib Hom complexes. Their homology maps identify, through homologyAddEquiv and CohomologyClass.homAddEquiv, with precomposition by p in the homotopy category. The localization map on morphisms into every shift of J is bijective because J is K-injective, and Q(p) is invertible. Thus this precomposition map is bijective, so ordinary sections of Hom(A,J)→Hom(P,J) is a quasi-isomorphism.

In the naturality square of the sections comparison for Hom(A,J)→Hom(P,J), both horizontal arrows and the comparison at Hom(P,J) are invertible. Consequently the comparison at Hom(A,J) is invertible. Its construction was natural before the auxiliary K-flat choice; assemble its components into a natural isomorphism and combine with the representative isomorphism. No boundedness or K-flatness of A and no exactness of products or sections is assumed.

Reuse the globalComplexIso and its naturality, whose components are the degreewise global-cochain maps, to give the stated global Hom complex and the formula for pre- and postcomposition. Finally, choose representatives of K and M and the functorial K-injective replacement of M. Apply derived homology to the sections isomorphism, identify homology of the external Hom complex with degree-n cohomology classes, identify these with morphisms into the shift of the target in the homotopy category, and use IsKInjective.Qh_map_bijective together with the localization shift isomorphism. Transport along the chosen representative isomorphisms to obtain the additive equivalence with Hom(K,M[n]).
